chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zur'ah, from Abu Basir, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'Guard yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is humans and stones.' I said: 'This is my soul that I am guarding, but how should I guard my family?' He replied: 'Instruct them to do what Allah has commanded, and forbid them from what Allah has forbidden. If they obey you, you will have guarded them; but if they disobey you, you will have fulfilled your responsibility.'
ai.seo_question: How does one practically guard their family from Hellfire according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* elucidates the mechanism of *Amr bi-l-Ma'ruf* (commanding good) within the domestic sphere, establishing that a guardian's duty is fulfilled through active instruction rather than guaranteed compliance. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on personal responsibility (*taklif*) in family management, where the parent's accountability is tied to their effort in conveying divine commands, regardless of the family members' eventual obedience or disobedience.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 13.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Zurʿah, from Abū Baṣīr who said,

“I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) about the verse wherein Allah, the Exalted, says: Guard yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is humans and stones (Q66:6), and said, ‘This is my soul that I am guarding, but how should I guard my family?’ He replied, ‘By instructing them to do as Allah has commanded, and forbidding them from what Allah has forbidden. Then if they obey you, you will have guarded them [from it], but if they disobey you, you will have fulfilled your responsibility.’”
